title: Repeated DNA Sequences
summary: Given a string s representing a DNA sequence composed of the nucleotides 'A', 'C', 'G', and 'T', return all 10-letter-long substrings that appear more than once within the sequence.
statement: Given a string s representing a DNA sequence composed of the nucleotides 'A', 'C', 'G', and 'T', return all 10-letter-long substrings that appear more than once within the sequence. The output order does not matter.
constraints: 1–100000 characters, each A, C, G, or T.
Return each distinct length-10 substring that occurs at least twice, in any order. Overlapping occurrences count. Each repeated sequence appears only once in the result.
target_space_complexity: O(min(len(s), 4^10)), including stored codes and output
hints: Every starting position can define a window, even if it overlaps a previous occurrence.
Track windows seen before and separately track those already included in the answer.
Encode each nucleotide in two bits; retain the last twenty bits. After ten characters, report a previously seen code only if it has not been reported yet.
Leading A characters encode as zero, so wait until the window really contains ten characters before testing the code.
editorial: A fixed ten-character DNA window fits exactly in twenty bits; the encoding has no collisions among windows of that length. Shifting in each new character and masking discards the oldest one. Separate seen and reported sets distinguish the first, second, and later occurrences. The independent oracle materializes and sorts all ten-character slices, then groups equal adjacent strings. Its comparisons include overlapping windows and preserve the requirement that each answer appear only once.

tests.explanation: Both 'AAAAACCCCC' and 'CCCCCAAAAA' occur twice; no other length-10 sequence repeats.
The ten-letter sequence 'AAAAAAAAAA' starts at four overlapping positions, but is returned only once.
